endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Throughout the AI tool’s lifecycle, the multidisciplinary development team shall analyse potential risks, assess each risk’s likelihood, effects and risk-benefit balance, define risk mitigation measures, monitor the risks and mitigations continuously, and maintain a risk management file.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: ID.RA-P1: Contextual factors related to the systems/products/ser vices and the data actions are identified (e.g., individuals’ demographics and privacy interests or perceptions, data sensitivity and/or types, visibility of data processing to individuals and third parties).

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: HDOs should periodically evaluate cumulative AI risk across all deployed systems, particularly where multiple AI solutions influence the same workflow, patient population, or workforce staff (e.g., clinicians, nurses, or other employees who participate in multiple AI-supported workflows simultaneously).

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology

endorsements.title: Best Practice Guidelines for Bioethical Use of Medical AI in Healthcare. An eDelphi Consensus Exercise
endorsements.quote: An impact assessment should be carried out prior to the implementation of each Medical-AI to make sure benefits outweigh the negative effects of using medical- AI

endorsements.title: Clinical use of artificial intelligence requires AI-capable organizations
endorsements.quote: We propose that similar impact statements should be created before AI-based tool deployment decisions are finalized.

endorsements.title: Practical consequences of the European union-AI act for anatomic pathology laboratories a European society of pathology and European society of digital and integrative pathology commissioned expert opinion paper
endorsements.issuer: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
endorsements.quote: Specifically, read together with the GDPR, it is arguable that the performance and documentation of a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) are necessary; furthermore, a fundamental rights assessment prior to AI implementation is required (Article 27).

endorsements.title: The EU AI Act: implications and compliance guidance for healthcare facilities
endorsements.quote: Crucially, the FRIA must address the GDPR interface.

evidence.title: Developer Perspectives on Potential Harms of Machine Learning Predictive Analytics in Health Care: Qualitative Analysis
evidence.outcome: Existence of robust procedures at developers to assess potential harms and need for mitigation
evidence.effect: Developers recognized harms to patients, public, and health systems, but robust procedures to assess harm potential and the need for mitigation do not exist.
evidence.quote: Even though MLPA developers recognized that their products can harm patients, public, and even health systems, robust procedures to assess the potential for harms and the need for mitigation do not exist.
evidence.sample_unit: developers (data scientists, software engineers, managers) interviewed

commentary.bottom_line: Seven guidance documents endorse AI impact assessments, but no study has tested whether conducting them reduces overlooked harms. One interview study of 40 U.S. developers found that formal procedures to assess harm potential were lacking, which documents the gap without showing that assessments close it.

perspectives.view: No study evaluates impact assessments as an intervention, so certainty is rated as no direct evidence. The one available study interviewed 40 developers in the United States. It shows that the hazard exists, since developers recognized harms but lacked formal procedures to assess them. It cannot show whether assessments change deployment decisions or patient outcomes.

Developers in the interview study named harms to patients, the public, and health systems, yet they described no formal process to judge harm potential or the need for mitigation. An impact assessment may surface these failure modes before deployment. No data show how often it catches harms that would otherwise reach patients.

Two European commentaries read Article 27 of the EU AI Act, together with the GDPR, as requiring a fundamental rights impact assessment and a data protection impact assessment before implementation. FUTURE-AI lists a lifecycle risk management file as a must. NIST AI 600-1 and CHAI present assessments as voluntary, so obligations differ by jurisdiction.

CHAI asks organizations to identify contextual factors such as individuals' demographics, which could direct attention to affected subgroups. The single hazard study interviewed developers rather than patients and reported no findings for Medicaid, safety-net, or limited English proficiency populations. Whether assessments detect harms concentrated in these groups remains untested.

The CHAI playbook asks organizations to evaluate cumulative risk across all deployed systems that share a workflow, patient population, or staff group, which extends the assessment beyond single tools. No supplied study reports the staff time, cost, or expertise that such assessments require, so organizations cannot estimate the burden from existing evidence.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare deployment decisions and post-deployment harm reports between organizations that conduct structured impact assessments and those that do not, and that measure the staff time and cost each assessment requires.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, and the one hazard study sampled developers without reporting on Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Organizations serving these groups have no evidence on whether impact assessments identify harms specific to their patients.
